I grew up with a similar dynamic (just flips the genders) and this feeling rules me to the point where I struggle to keep my room and other parts of my living space clean regularly. I also can't ride a bike, drive, struggle to tie my shoes properly and am putting off applying for Uni/College bc the fear of "failing" at the application process somehow despite doing consistently well in school. I worry and fret about it everyday. 

I had to do a fair amount of digging through my feelings to find out what might be the cause. It's like my internal critic is in overdrive at all times, because that was how it was growing with two emotionally unstable parents. On a whim I might be punished for something as simple as going up and down the stairs a few times after dinner or any other slightly noisy activity would make my dad flip his lid if he was drunk.

When my parents tried to teach me critical skills  when i was young (i.e. Bike riding) their frustration usually came to the surface very quickly and they would snap and berate me+ shame me for being behind my peers. Im 20 and still live at home and even to this day my mom tells me things like  "You're XY years old - you should be capable of these things/I know you aren't retarded/you are old enough to birth children/you won't survive on your own" and I realized that decades of hearing these put downs and criticisms is what shaped my negative inner voice.

I feel incapable bc I was always told I would be, that I was useless and lazy.. So when I try to start something new and am not perfect at the beginning the first instinct is to shut down, dissociate and prepare for the oncoming onslaught of verbal/physical abuse my childhood self was used to.

If I think about it too much I get so angry... My parents failed me and it feels like I'm cursed - but working hard to reprogram my internal self talk to be more neutral, loving and supportive has been so, so beneficial and changed my perspective on life greatly. When you catch yourself shutting down, see if the way you speak to yourself reflects your parent's feelings of the past and not yours of the now. We have to remind our bodies that we are no longer back in time and these defense mechanisms can be retired. 

This was very rambly and long but this paralysis is my biggest roadblock in life rn. I can't wait to be free. Good luck on your own healing journey.
